title: How Putin Made North Korea Richer and More Dangerous
summary: A Korea expert explains how arms and troops for Russia's war revived North Korea's economy and strengthened its nuclear and military position.

assertions.quote: it's fast becoming a dangerous regional power in its own right with a nuclear arsenal that can threaten the continental United States

verdicts.note: North Korea's arsenal, missile range and Russian backing are at their peak, but greater capability is not the same as a greater intent to fight.
SIPRI describes a growing arsenal (about 60 warheads, accelerating fissile production, new ICBMs), which supports a rising capability but not a judgment that overall danger is at an all-time high.
CFR's survey moved North Korea up to Tier I in 2026 because a resumption of nuclear tests could trigger armed confrontation, a rising concern but no all-time comparison.

verdicts.note: North Korea's 2022 nuclear forces law allows preemptive nuclear use in a range of scenarios.
SIPRI notes North Korea's 2022 nuclear-use law allows pre-emptive nuclear use in the event of an attack, including by a non-nuclear-armed state.

verdicts.note: US intelligence judges North Korea strongly committed to expanding its nuclear arsenal and strategic weapons to solidify its deterrent, which offers no sign it will disarm.
